children: Inflation in Taiwan is likely to have stayed elevated in September amid higher energy prices and strong domestic demand. The island's consumer prices likely rose 2.4% from a year earlier, according to a poll of six economists polled by The Wall Street Journal. While the rebound in oil prices have lifted transport costs, the earlier arrival of the Mid-Autumn Festival this year may have boosted food and services prices, DBS economists say. After the Taiwan central bank stood pat for another quarter in September despite rising inflation, markets will closely watch the next inflation reports ahead of the December decision meeting. DBS expects a modest 12.5bp hike for the policy rate to 2.125% in December. (sherry.qin@wsj.com)
